profile.name: Jun Tan
profile.specialism: Mechatronics engineer and machine learning researcher
profile.introduction: I develop intelligent systems across robotics, embedded software and machine learning. My work spans engineering roles at Dyson, Allye Energy and Mercedes-AMG HPP, followed by an MSc in Applied Machine Learning at Imperial College London.
profile.story: My engineering journey began with international robotics competitions, including the IYRC Open Maker title in 2017. At Southampton, I developed that practical experience through mechatronics, Formula Student and research into rehabilitation robotics. Industry roles took me into product testing, energy storage and Formula 1 powertrain software. I then completed postgraduate study in applied machine learning at Imperial, bringing my interests in physical systems and intelligent software together.
profile.title: Engineering & Machine Learning

ML systems work spanning LoRA, neural architecture search, quantisation and CUDA kernels.

projects.title: Autonomous Navigation Rover
projects.summary: A six-wheel autonomous rover developed in three months on a £130 budget, integrating mechanical design, electronics and embedded control.

sections.heading: Project overview
sections.text: As technical lead, I led the development of an autonomous rover capable of navigating obstacles and uneven terrain. The team designed and built the system within a three-month schedule and a £130 budget.

sections.heading: Mechanical and electrical design
sections.text: The drivetrain used six worm-geared motors for high torque. The chassis combined custom 3D-printed and laser-cut parts with aluminium motor supports. Power distribution circuits supplied the motor drivers and electronics from a LiPo battery.

sections.heading: Navigation and control
sections.text: A C++ path-planning algorithm on an Arduino Mega processed LIDAR measurements. An MPU6050 gyroscope provided heading feedback, with PID correction compensating for uneven motor output. The project also incorporated SLAM techniques for narrow environments and automatic headlights.

projects.result: The rover navigated obstacles and rough terrain successfully. The project received the highest mark recorded for the module, as documented in the engineering portfolio.

projects.title: Glove-based Invisible Keyboard
projects.summary: A wearable input system that uses motion and force sensors with deep learning to predict typed characters.

sections.heading: Project overview
sections.text: The Glove-based Invisible Keyboard project investigated typing on a surface without a physical keyboard. Sensor-equipped gloves captured finger and hand movements for live character prediction.

sections.heading: Sensor integration
sections.text: Arduino Nano BLE Sense Rev2 controllers, inertial sensors and force-sensitive resistors recorded hand motion and surface contact. The resulting input contained 118 dimensions of sensor data.

sections.heading: Learning and inference
sections.text: The custom REFFCO architecture combined an attention LSTM with language model fusion. Optuna supported hyperparameter tuning, and a live inference pipeline processed sensor readings to predict characters during typing.

projects.result: The project integrated embedded sensing, data processing and deep learning into a live character prediction pipeline.
projects.image_description: A schematic summary of the system: glove sensor measurements are processed by an attention LSTM and combined with a language model to predict characters.
projects.preview: Translating hand movement into typed characters.

projects.title: Q-LEAC Stroke Rehabilitation System
projects.summary: A reinforcement learning controller combining electrical muscle stimulation and camera feedback for stroke rehabilitation.

sections.heading: Research objective
sections.text: My BEng dissertation investigated Q-learning as a control approach for forearm muscle stimulation in stroke rehabilitation, compared with a traditional model-based controller.

sections.heading: System implementation
sections.text: I developed a MATLAB–C++ system in which a Q-learning controller selected stimulation actions and an UltraLeap camera measured movement. The feedback loop supported real-time control.

sections.heading: Evaluation
sections.text: The system was tested with patients in a hospital setting. The evaluation considered the live training time required by the controller relative to the model-based approach.

projects.result: Q-LEAC reduced live controller training time by more than 50% compared with the traditional model-based method. This result concerns controller training time and does not measure clinical recovery.
projects.image_description: The control loop links a Q-learning controller to forearm stimulation and UltraLeap movement tracking. Camera measurements provide feedback for subsequent control actions.
projects.preview: Learning a controller for rehabilitation robotics.

projects.title: Mase EDGE: Android Model Optimisation
projects.summary: A hardware-in-the-loop pipeline for adapting deep neural networks to Android devices using measured device feedback.

sections.heading: Project objective
sections.text: Mase EDGE addressed the deployment of deep neural networks on Android hardware. The objective was to select model and execution settings using feedback from the target device.

sections.heading: Optimisation pipeline
sections.text: I developed a pipeline using Optuna to search model and execution parameters, including CPU, GPU and NPU backend delegation ratios. The workflow also incorporated quantisation-aware training, post-training quantisation and pruning.

sections.heading: Device evaluation
sections.text: The optimisation study used real-time feedback from the model running in the Android app. This enabled deployment decisions to account for the specifications and behaviour of the target device.

projects.result: The pipeline automated the search for device-specific model and execution configurations, combining model optimisation with hardware measurements.
projects.image_description: The optimisation workflow searches configurations with Optuna, deploys them to an Android device and uses measured feedback to guide the next search.
projects.preview: Adapting neural networks to real Android hardware.

projects.title: Formula Student Driver Controls
projects.summary: Driver controls development for an electric Formula Student car, covering cockpit integration, structural analysis and component manufacture.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text: As a driver controls engineer for Southampton University Formula Student, I worked on the integration of the team’s electric vehicle. The design changes aimed to improve the driver’s experience and accommodate a larger accumulator behind the cockpit.

sections.heading: Design and analysis
sections.text: I redesigned the steering rack cover in SOLIDWORKS and evaluated its structural performance in ANSYS. The work also covered steering, seating and firewall positions, brake pedal weight reduction, and dashboard integration for battery information, brake bias and DRS controls.

sections.heading: Manufacture and testing
sections.text: I gained experience with carbon fibre wet lay-up, laser-cut moulds and waterjet-cut pedal structures. Vehicle testing included high-voltage tractive system verification, CAN bus monitoring and pedal telemetry.

projects.result: The steering rack cover’s structural strength and safety factor improved by 32%. The steering and seat system moved forward by 75 mm, and the brake pedal mass decreased by 15% while maintaining an arm safety factor above 2.5.

projects.title: IoT Quarantine Recorder
projects.summary: An Arduino-based prototype for collecting temperature and heartbeat readings and transmitting them to a central monitoring device.

sections.heading: Project objective
sections.text: I developed the Quarantine Recorder during COVID-19 to support the collection of temperature and heartbeat readings in quarantine centres. The prototype aimed to reduce manual monitoring work.

sections.heading: Hardware and communication
sections.text: An Arduino Uno collected measurements from temperature and heartbeat sensors. An ESP8266 transmitted the readings to a main device for central monitoring.

projects.result: The prototype received the Innovative Maker Award and Most Market Value Award at the online NRL 2020 event.

projects.title: Task-based Transfer Reinforcement Learning
projects.summary: MSc dissertation research into contrastive representations and F-N-B factorisation for knowledge reuse across reinforcement learning tasks.

sections.heading: Research objective
sections.text: My MSc dissertation investigated how an agent could reuse learned knowledge across tasks to address sample efficiency and training time in high-dimensional reinforcement learning.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: The research explored task-based transfer reinforcement learning through contrastive representations and a custom F-N-B factorisation. It focused on few-shot and zero-shot transfer, including representation learning independent of a particular reward function.

sections.heading: Research context
sections.text: The dissertation built on research around ExORL and OGBench. The implementation toolset included PyTorch and MuJoCo, alongside reinforcement learning methods such as SAC, TD3 and PPO.

projects.result: The dissertation examined representation learning and task information as a basis for transferring knowledge between reinforcement learning tasks.
projects.image_description: An illustration of the research approach: contrastive exploration, F-N-B factorisation and transfer to new tasks.

projects.title: Transformer Simulation and Optimisation
projects.summary: Finite element analysis of a single-phase transformer, investigating eddy current losses and simulation efficiency.

sections.heading: Project objective
sections.text: This project explored a single-phase isolation transformer, with a focus on eddy current losses, unknown circuit parameters and the computational cost of simulation.

sections.heading: Simulation method
sections.text: I modelled virtual lamination through effective conductivity and permeability matrices, studied current density and flux distribution, and used short-circuit and open-circuit tests to identify circuit parameters. Exploiting geometric symmetry reduced the simulation domain.

projects.result: Exploiting symmetry reduced simulation time from eight minutes to 59 seconds. The virtual lamination study reduced core current density by 87%.

gallery.caption: Current density distribution from the transformer simulation
gallery.description: The simulated current density distribution used to investigate losses and the effect of core lamination.

projects.image_description: The COMSOL geometry of the single-phase transformer used for the electromagnetic simulation.

projects.title: Electromagnetic Actuator Design
projects.summary: Electromagnetic design and finite element analysis of an actuator specified to deliver 750 N across a 7 mm air gap.

sections.heading: Design requirements
sections.text: Design a magnetic actuator capable of providing 750 N of force when the plunger is separated by a 7 mm air gap, while keeping the magnetic material below saturation.

sections.heading: Analysis
sections.text: I constructed the geometry and electromagnetic model in COMSOL, used symmetry to reduce computation, and carried out a mesh refinement study. I compared analytical and simulation results while exploring how plunger geometry affected force as the air gap increased.

projects.result: The final simulation achieved 766 N while keeping the magnetic material below saturation.
projects.image_description: The simulated magnetic flux distribution in the actuator, used to assess force generation and magnetic saturation.
projects.preview: Engineering an actuator for a 750 N target.

projects.title: Ball Screw Drivetrain Design
projects.summary: Motion profiling, component sizing and CAD design for a ball screw drive in an aerospace test system.

sections.heading: Design requirements
sections.text: Develop a drive system for a test article undergoing rapid repeated motion. The design needed a motion profile, a suitable motor and a reliable method of measuring and limiting travel.

sections.heading: Design and component sizing
sections.text: I generated a cubic polynomial motion profile in MATLAB, calculated peak and continuous torque from the system inertia, and sized the motor and encoders. Datum and limit switches supported safe operation, with a SOLIDWORKS assembly bringing the components together.

projects.result: The final design package included motion and torque calculations, motor and encoder selections, and manufacturing drawings.

projects.image_description: The CAD model of the ball screw drivetrain, including the motor, coupling, screw and test article support.

projects.title: NXP Camera-guided Robot
projects.summary: Chassis design, rapid prototyping and drivetrain integration for a camera-guided competition robot.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text: For the NXP Intelligence Car Challenge at Southampton, my main responsibility was designing and manufacturing the robot’s structure and supporting drivetrain integration.

sections.heading: Hardware design
sections.text: I designed a chassis with dedicated positions for motors, gears, batteries and circuit boards. A lightweight 3D-printed base and acrylic upper plate supported the processor, with cooling fans, custom silicone tyres and BLDC motor control.

sections.heading: System integration
sections.text: The team’s vision pipeline used Python, OpenCV and NumPy for track boundary detection. My mechanical and drivetrain work supported camera-guided navigation and closed-loop speed control.

projects.result: The project provided practical experience in rapid prototyping, custom circuitry and BLDC drivetrain integration for camera-based navigation.

projects.title: RFID Reader PCB
projects.summary: Circuit simulation, PCB layout, assembly and testing of an RFID tag reader.

sections.heading: Circuit design
sections.text: I designed an RFID tag reader with antenna and demodulation circuitry. NI Multisim supported the filter, amplifier, power supply and detector simulations before the board layout was created in Autodesk EAGLE.

sections.heading: PCB implementation
sections.text: I created custom footprints for the LCD and buzzer, arranged and routed the components, and separated analogue and digital circuitry to limit signal distortion. After university manufacturing, I soldered the components and validated the board on the bench.

projects.result: The manufactured board successfully detected RFID tags at multiple distances during bench testing.

projects.title: FPGA Computer Architecture
projects.summary: A simple computer implemented in SystemVerilog, covering instruction execution, arithmetic and memory operations.

sections.heading: Project overview
sections.text: In my first year, I modelled a simple computer using SystemVerilog on an Altera FPGA. The resulting system was used to encrypt and decrypt strings of letters.

sections.heading: Computer architecture
sections.text: A three-bit opcode and five-bit address formed an eight-bit bus protocol. Registers, tri-state buffers, an ALU and a synchronising clock supported the instruction cycle, with simulation in Quartus and ModelSim. ROM held instructions while RAM stored variables and results.

projects.result: The FPGA implementation performed basic computer operations, including address loading and ALU arithmetic, and was used for string encryption and decryption.

projects.title: Competition Robotics
projects.summary: Humanoid, omnidirectional and sumo robot projects developed for national and international competitions.

sections.heading: Robot platforms
sections.text: Humanoid dancing and boxing introduced servo coordination, balance and inverse kinematics. Mecanum and omnidirectional robots brought new challenges in weight distribution and movement, while football robots combined infrared ball detection with compass navigation.

sections.heading: Sumo robot development
sections.text: I designed robust steel chassis, worked with high-torque worm-geared DC motors and used Arduino control with Cytron motor drivers. Remote-controlled versions mapped controller inputs to driving modes; autonomous versions used ultrasonic and infrared sensing to locate opponents and stay inside the arena.

projects.result: Competition results included wins at Singapore Open 2019 and KLESF 2019 sumo events, and second place in humanoid boxing at myMaker 2019.

projects.title: Language Model Optimisation
projects.summary: Language model optimisation using MXINT4 quantisation-aware training, the Muon optimiser and unstructured pruning.

sections.heading: Optimisation techniques
sections.text: For the OpenAI Parameter Golf Challenge, I worked on language model optimisation using XSA, MXINT4-based quantisation-aware training, the Muon optimiser and unstructured pruning.

sections.heading: Project focus
sections.text: The work examined how training algorithms, numerical precision and pruning affect the representation and optimisation of a language model.

projects.result: The project explored training, quantisation and pruning techniques for efficient language model representation.
projects.image_description: An illustration of the model optimisation techniques: training with Muon, MXINT4 quantisation and weight pruning.
